extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large unified database of human motion capture data that combines 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common SMPL-based representation using MoSh++, including body shape, pose, soft-tissue dynamics, and articulated hands.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by unifying 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets using MoSh++. A novel synchronized scans-and-markers dataset (SSM) was additionally collected for hyperparameter tuning and evaluation using an OptiTrack mocap system synchronized with a 4D scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that during mocap sessions markers may get occluded by the body, and that some datasets had swapped and mislabeled markers that were manually inspected and corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based mocap datasets from ACCAD, BioMotion, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions; plus synchronized 4D body scans and mocap markers for SSM.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ converts sparse mocap markers into SMPL/SMPL-H body model parameters, including shape, pose, soft-tissue dynamics, and hand articulation. The paper also states that problematic swapped or mislabeled markers were manually inspected and either corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source datasets were unified into a single SMPL-based format. For SSM, subjects wore minimal clothing and markers were placed directly on the skin where possible. The paper also describes separating sequences into training, validation, and test sets for hyperparameter tuning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: AMASS is publicly available to the research community and the authors state they will continue to expand the dataset and support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape, pose, hand articulation, soft-tissue motion, and mocap-derived subject information; the dataset includes subjects and motions, but the paper does not explicitly report demographics such as age, gender, or ethnicity.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning and computer vision, and the authors mention potential use for synthetic training data and denoising mocap data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing mocap datasets are often narrowly focused on particular motion classes and vary in markersets and laboratory-specific procedures; AMASS inherits the composition of those archival datasets and includes only the motions and subjects present there.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. It also notes that hand articulation evaluation lacks ground-truth data, and that allowing too many shape components can overfit to mocap markers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training data for deep learning, animation, visualization, computer vision, pose and motion reconstruction, and denoising mocap data.
